blood pressure is no longer affected at all
harmful waste can accumulate in the blood
the bladder takes over filtering the blood
questions.explain: 신장이 기능을 못하면 혈액에 노폐물이 쌓인다고 했으므로 'harmful waste can accumulate in the blood'가 정답이다.

title: The Science of Hydration
passage: Water makes up more than half of the human body and takes part in nearly every process that keeps a person alive. It carries nutrients to cells, removes waste, cushions joints, and helps regulate body temperature through sweat. Because the body constantly loses water through breathing, sweating, and waste, this supply must be replaced regularly. When fluid loss is not replaced, dehydration can set in, producing thirst, fatigue, dizziness, and, in serious cases, dangerous drops in blood pressure. Sweat contains not only water but also electrolytes—minerals such as sodium and potassium that help nerves and muscles work properly. During long or intense exercise, replacing these minerals as well as water can help the body function and prevent cramps. For most everyday activity, however, plain water is enough, and the common advice to drink when thirsty serves many people well. Drinking far more than the body needs offers no extra benefit and, in rare cases, can even be harmful.

questions.q: The main idea of this passage is that
options: electrolytes are always more important than water
people should drink as much water as they possibly can
water is essential to many body functions and must be replaced as it is lost
dehydration only occurs during intense exercise
questions.explain: 지문은 물이 여러 신체 기능에 필수적이며 잃은 만큼 보충해야 한다고 설명하므로 'water is essential to many body functions and must be replaced as it is lost'가 정답이다.

questions.q: According to the passage, electrolytes such as sodium and potassium
options: help nerves and muscles work properly
are found only in plain water
cause dehydration during exercise
remove the body's need for water
questions.explain: 전해질은 신경과 근육이 제대로 작동하도록 돕는다고 했으므로 'help nerves and muscles work properly'가 정답이다.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that for a short, ordinary walk, a person
options: needs a special electrolyte drink
can usually stay hydrated with plain water
should avoid drinking any water
will inevitably become dehydrated
questions.explain: 일상적 활동에는 맹물로 충분하다고 했으므로 짧은 산책에는 'can usually stay hydrated with plain water'가 정답이다.

questions.q: In this passage, the word "regulate" most nearly means
options: raise sharply
measure exactly
remove entirely
control or keep steady
questions.explain: regulate body temperature는 체온을 조절해 일정하게 유지한다는 의미이므로 'control or keep steady'가 정답이다.

title: The Many Tasks of the Liver
passage: The liver is the largest internal organ in the human body and one of the most versatile. Positioned in the upper right of the abdomen, it carries out hundreds of functions that keep the body running smoothly. One of its best-known jobs is filtering the blood that leaves the stomach and intestines, breaking down harmful substances, including alcohol and certain drugs, before they can spread. The liver also produces bile, a fluid that helps the body digest fats, and it stores energy in the form of a sugar called glycogen, releasing it when the body needs fuel. In addition, the liver makes proteins that help blood clot and regulates the levels of many chemicals in the bloodstream. Remarkably, the liver can regenerate: if part of it is removed or damaged, the remaining tissue can grow back to nearly its original size. This ability makes living-donor transplants possible, but it does not protect the organ from long-term harm.

questions.q: According to the passage, the liver produces bile in order to
options: help the blood clot after an injury
help the body digest fats
store energy as glycogen
filter alcohol out of the blood
questions.explain: 간은 지방 소화를 돕는 담즙(bile)을 만든다고 했으므로 'help the body digest fats'가 정답이다.

questions.q: In this passage, the word "regenerate" most nearly means
options: filter out waste
shut down completely
produce more bile
grow back or renew itself
questions.explain: regenerate는 손상된 조직이 다시 자라 재생된다는 뜻이므로 'grow back or renew itself'가 정답이다.

questions.q: The main idea of this passage is that
options: the liver's only role is to digest fats
the liver cannot be damaged in any way
the liver is a versatile organ that performs many vital functions and can regenerate
living-donor transplants are the liver's main purpose
questions.explain: 지문은 간이 여러 필수 기능을 하고 재생할 수 있는 다재다능한 장기라고 설명하므로 'a versatile organ that performs many vital functions and can regenerate'가 정답이다.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that a person who drinks a large amount of alcohol relies on the liver to
options: break down the alcohol before it spreads through the body
produce additional red blood cells
increase the body's store of bile
keep the liver itself from ever being harmed
questions.explain: 간은 알코올 같은 해로운 물질을 퍼지기 전에 분해한다고 했으므로 'break down the alcohol before it spreads through the body'가 정답이다.

title: Why Muscles Get Sore
passage: Many people notice that a day or two after unfamiliar or strenuous exercise, their muscles feel stiff and tender. This delayed discomfort, known as delayed-onset muscle soreness, typically appears from twenty-four to seventy-two hours after the activity rather than during it. For many years, people blamed the buildup of lactic acid, but scientists now understand that lactic acid clears from the muscles within an hour or so and is not the cause. Instead, the soreness results from tiny tears in the muscle fibers, especially during movements in which the muscle lengthens under load, such as running downhill or lowering a weight. The body responds to this microscopic damage with inflammation as it repairs the tissue, and the healing process makes the muscles stronger over time. Gentle movement, stretching, and rest can ease the discomfort, which usually fades within a few days. Notably, the same workout tends to cause much less soreness once the body has adapted to it.

questions.q: The main idea of this passage is that
options: delayed muscle soreness comes from tiny tears in muscle fibers, not from lactic acid
lactic acid is the main cause of muscle soreness
exercise should be avoided in order to prevent soreness
muscle soreness never improves with continued training
questions.explain: 지문은 지연성 근육통이 젖산이 아니라 근섬유의 미세한 파열에서 비롯된다고 설명하므로 'tiny tears in muscle fibers, not from lactic acid'가 정답이다.

questions.q: According to the passage, delayed-onset muscle soreness usually appears
options: during the exercise itself
within one hour of finishing exercise
about one to three days after the exercise
only after several weeks have passed
questions.explain: 지연성 근육통은 운동 후 24~72시간, 즉 약 1~3일 뒤에 나타난다고 했으므로 'about one to three days after the exercise'가 정답이다.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that repeating the same workout regularly will
options: cause increasingly severe soreness each time
tend to produce less soreness as the body adapts
permanently damage the muscle fibers
prevent the muscles from ever getting stronger
questions.explain: 몸이 적응하면 같은 운동은 근육통을 훨씬 덜 유발한다고 했으므로 'tend to produce less soreness as the body adapts'가 정답이다.

questions.q: In this passage, the word "strenuous" most nearly means
options: relaxing and easy
extremely brief
familiar and routine
demanding great effort
questions.explain: strenuous exercise는 큰 힘이 드는 격렬한 운동을 뜻하므로 'demanding great effort'가 정답이다.

title: How the Body Uses Protein
passage: Protein is one of the nutrients the body needs in large amounts, and it serves as a basic building material for living tissue. When a person eats protein-rich foods such as meat, eggs, beans, or dairy, the digestive system breaks the protein down into smaller units called amino acids. The body then reassembles these amino acids into the many different proteins it needs to build and repair muscles, organs, skin, and other tissues, as well as to make enzymes and some hormones. There are twenty amino acids in all. The body can produce many of them on its own, but nine, known as essential amino acids, must come from food. Animal foods generally supply all nine, while most plant foods lack one or more; for this reason, people who eat only plants can combine different sources, such as beans and grains, to obtain the full set. Unlike fat, the body cannot store extra protein for later, so a regular supply is important.

questions.q: According to the passage, essential amino acids are those that
options: the body can make on its own
are found only in beans and grains
the body stores for later use
must be obtained from food
questions.explain: 필수 아미노산은 음식에서 얻어야 하는 것이라고 했으므로 'must be obtained from food'가 정답이다.

questions.q: The main idea of this passage is that
options: only animal foods contain any protein
protein is broken into amino acids that the body uses to build and repair tissue
the body can store extra protein indefinitely
plant foods cannot provide any amino acids
questions.explain: 지문은 단백질이 아미노산으로 분해되어 조직을 만들고 수리하는 데 쓰인다고 설명하므로 'protein is broken into amino acids that the body uses to build and repair tissue'가 정답이다.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that a person who eats only plant foods
options: can still obtain all essential amino acids by combining different plant sources
cannot get any essential amino acids at all
does not need protein of any kind
must eat meat in order to survive
questions.explain: 식물만 먹는 사람도 콩과 곡물처럼 여러 식물 공급원을 조합해 필수 아미노산을 모두 얻을 수 있다고 했으므로 'can still obtain all essential amino acids by combining different plant sources'가 정답이다.

questions.q: In this passage, the word "reassembles" most nearly means
options: breaks apart
stores away
puts back together
digests very slowly
questions.explain: reassemble은 아미노산을 다시 조립해 단백질을 만든다는 의미이므로 'puts back together'가 정답이다.

title: The Inner Ear and Balance
passage: Balance feels effortless, yet it depends on a remarkable sensing system hidden deep within the ear. Beyond its role in hearing, the inner ear contains a structure called the vestibular system, which detects motion and helps the body stay upright. Its key parts are three fluid-filled loops called the semicircular canals, set at different angles. When the head turns, the fluid inside them shifts and bends tiny hair cells, which send signals to the brain about the direction and speed of movement. Other nearby structures sense the pull of gravity and straight-line motion, such as riding in a car. The brain combines these signals with information from the eyes and from sensors in the muscles and joints to build a clear sense of position and keep the body steady. When these sources disagree—for example, when a person reads in a moving vehicle—the mismatch can produce the queasy feeling known as motion sickness.

questions.q: According to the passage, the semicircular canals detect movement by
options: measuring changes in air pressure
sensing light that enters through the eyes
shifting fluid that bends tiny hair cells
producing sound waves inside the ear
questions.explain: 반고리관은 내부 액체가 움직여 미세한 털세포를 굽히면서 움직임을 감지한다고 했으므로 'shifting fluid that bends tiny hair cells'가 정답이다.

questions.q: The main idea of this passage is that
options: the inner ear's vestibular system helps the body sense motion and maintain balance
the inner ear is used only for hearing
motion sickness cannot be explained by science
balance depends entirely on the eyes
questions.explain: 지문은 내이의 전정기관이 움직임을 감지하고 균형을 유지하도록 돕는다고 설명하므로 'the inner ear's vestibular system helps the body sense motion and maintain balance'가 정답이다.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that motion sickness results when
options: the semicircular canals stop working entirely
both the eyes and the ears shut down
the inner ear produces too much fluid
signals from the eyes and the inner ear disagree
questions.explain: 눈과 내이의 신호가 서로 어긋날 때 멀미가 생긴다고 했으므로 'signals from the eyes and the inner ear disagree'가 정답이다.

questions.q: In this passage, the word "queasy" most nearly means
options: dizzy with joy
nauseated or sick to the stomach
perfectly steady
unusually alert
questions.explain: queasy feeling은 멀미로 속이 메스꺼운 상태를 뜻하므로 'nauseated or sick to the stomach'가 정답이다.

title: Blood Types and Transfusion
passage: Human blood is not all the same; it comes in different types, and knowing a patient's type is vital before a transfusion. The most familiar system, called ABO, sorts blood into four groups—A, B, AB, and O—based on molecules called antigens found on the surface of red blood cells. The immune system learns to accept its own antigens but attacks any that are foreign, so mixing incompatible blood can cause a dangerous reaction in which cells clump together. People with type O blood have no A or B antigens, which lets their red cells be given safely to almost anyone, earning them the label "universal donors." Those with type AB, having both antigens, can receive red cells from any ABO type. A second system, the Rh factor, adds a positive or negative sign to each type. Before any transfusion, hospitals carefully test and match blood so that a patient receives cells the body will not reject.

questions.q: According to the passage, ABO blood groups are determined by
options: the Rh factor alone
antigens on the surface of red blood cells
the total number of red blood cells in the body
the speed at which the blood clots
questions.explain: ABO 혈액형은 적혈구 표면의 항원에 따라 나뉜다고 했으므로 'antigens on the surface of red blood cells'가 정답이다.

questions.q: It can be inferred from the passage that a patient with type AB blood
options: can donate red cells to anyone but receive from no one
has no antigens at all on its red blood cells
cannot safely receive a transfusion of any kind
can receive red cells from any ABO blood type
questions.explain: AB형은 두 항원을 모두 가져 어떤 ABO 유형의 적혈구도 받을 수 있다고 했으므로 'can receive red cells from any ABO blood type'가 정답이다.

questions.q: In this passage, the word "incompatible" most nearly means
options: freshly donated
perfectly matched
unable to be safely combined
unusually rich in antigens
questions.explain: incompatible blood은 안전하게 섞일 수 없는 피를 뜻하므로 'unable to be safely combined'가 정답이다.

questions.q: The author's primary purpose in this passage is to
options: explain how blood types differ and why matching them matters for transfusions
argue that type O blood is the healthiest blood type
describe the history of the first blood transfusion
warn readers against ever donating blood
questions.explain: 글의 목적은 혈액형이 어떻게 다르고 수혈 시 왜 일치가 중요한지 설명하는 것이므로 'explain how blood types differ and why matching them matters for transfusions'가 정답이다.
